1. Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term (1-3 days) after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral.  
2. When sentiment is negative (avg < 0), model tends to underestimate true price drops; adjust downward by 2–5% of recent 7-day average.  
3. After a price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 10–15% of peak value.  
4. Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 14-day average, reduce by 5–8% to align with historical reversion.  
5. Sentiment +1.0–0.5 correlates with 3–5 day price uptick; if sentiment is high, model should not overreact to short-term volatility — cap forecast increase at 3% above prior 7-day mean.  
6. If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often undercorrects — add 1–3% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.  
7. Model underperforms in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more in 3 consecutive days) — increase forecast by 2–4% to account for lagged sentiment effects.
